subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Bicycle: A Compound Machine Masterpiece
description: One-minute skill: The Bicycle: A Compound Machine Masterpiece.

hook.text: A bicycle uses levers, wheels, axles, gears, pulleys, and screws — all in one elegant frame.

buildup.text: Pedals are cranks. The chain is a belt drive. Handbrakes are levers. The derailleur shifts gear ratios.

discovery.text: A bike is about 99% efficient. Almost all your leg energy reaches the rear wheel. Cars manage about 30%.

twist.text: The bicycle wasn't perfected until the 1880s. The key invention was the chain drive, not the wheel.

climax.text: It remains the most energy-efficient form of human transport ever invented. Nothing else comes close.

punchline.text: Six simple machines in one frame. Peak engineering.

quiz.question: What makes the bicycle uniquely efficient?
options: Its lightweight frame reduces air resistance to near zero
About 99% of the rider's energy reaches the rear wheel
The pneumatic tires eliminate all rolling friction
